priorStories.headline: Microsoft outage disrupts Outlook and other services
priorStories.body:
An outage disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 365 services Thursday. Microsoft said some servers unexpectedly became unavailable, straining the remaining infrastructure.

By 6:57 p.m. Eastern, the company reported limited recovery after returning some servers to service and rerouting traffic. Full restoration had not been established in that update.

Nearly 130,000 Outlook reports appeared on Downdetector near the earlier peak. Those were user reports, not a verified count of affected accounts.

priorStories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
priorStories.body:
Nvidia said Thursday that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive and that chief financial officer Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO. His departure followed disclosures of extramarital relationships.

The board named Harvey C. Jones chairman and said it would consider both internal and external candidates for a permanent chief executive.

candidates.summary: Microsoft reported early stabilization and capacity improvements on November 13 as recovery work continued on the Microsoft 365 outage that began November 12. Full restoration had not been established. Earlier recovery attempts had not worked as expected, and the disruption continued to affect Outlook, Teams and other services. Microsoft said it had no indication that malicious activity caused the outage.
candidates.title: Microsoft reports early stabilization as global service outage continues
